correctness.rationale: All quantifiers finite m≥1 and d≥1, diameter≤ε. Convex-hull invariance makes every edge active. Hub/leaf step identities and conditional E,T,M moments follow by direct algebra. A=M²+aE+bT has vanishing one-step conditional drift for symbolic m. E converges geometrically in expectation to zero; M is a bounded martingale and converges to the common opinion. Bounded convergence and polarization yield the exact covariance, and equal-leaf substitution gives coefficient 1/18. Reproducible rational checks independently test 872 identities, but the infinite conclusion rests on proof.

value.rationale: The exact limiting consensus uncertainty is motivated by the published focus on convergence but absence of a variance law for an irregular social network. Stars are the natural extreme heterogeneous hub-and-spoke graph. The result identifies a nonzero 1/18 large-population variance with one disagreeing hub, distinguishing eventual agreement from reliable aggregation. The two-term covariance decomposes individual deviations and collective imbalance for all initial configurations, providing a rigorous nonconcentration mechanism rather than a narrow arbitrary numerical slice.
